note:
LISTEN FOR 0:36 (the band comes in on the pulse the two reeds are already making), then 1:05, 1:34 and 2:03 (the same band in five, seven and three to the bar, by retuning one reed), and 3:01 to the end (the hair is halved three times and the strokes come further apart). v1, CLOSE ENOUGH: THE WHOLE SHAPE STANDING, BARE (the song I wanted to make; chirper-two). Not checked by ear: everything below is measurement or intent.

THE IDEA. Two notes a hair apart make a pulse, as many times a second as the hair is wide in cycles; and each overtone of the pair is twice, three, four times as far apart, so it pulses twice, three, four times as fast. One mistuned unison is a polyrhythm, 1:2:3:4, with nobody playing it. Two harmoniums hold one note; the second is sharp by a width chosen in CYCLES so that the pulse is in tempo (66 to the minute: 1.1 Hz, eleven cents at F3, is once a beat). The band plays what the pair is doing: kick on the notes' own pulse (the bass holds from kick to kick), guitars twice as fast, toms three times, hat four times. The snare is outside the rule, on two and four. So the metre is a tuning and the form is a list of widths: in tune 0:00; a hair (a quarter of a pulse to the beat) 0:07.3; wider (a half) 0:21.8; square (one: common time, 4, 8, 12, 16 to the bar) 0:36.4; five (5, 10, 15, 20) on A flat 1:05.5; seven (7, 14, 21, 28) on B 1:34.5; three (3, 6, 9, 12) on the low E flat 2:03.6; square again 2:32.7; a half, a quarter, an eighth 3:01.8, 3:09.1, 3:16.4; in tune, one chord, 3:23.6. 58 bars, 3:30.9, 2800 notes on ten tracks. compose/chirpers10/motifs.md has the table.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. (1) The pair alone, whole song, raw seed 0: in every section of four bars or more each of the first four overtones' strongest slow pulse sits at its multiple of the hair (0.990 to 1.012 of it), 12.7 to 18.0 dB deep, its peaks within 0.09 of a pulse of the band's stroke. That was NOT so with the library harmonium as it comes: it beats with itself (a second reed 7 cents sharp) and its bellows tremble at 1.3 Hz, and in square the second harmonic's strongest pulse was at 1.37 Hz, not the hair's 2.2. The song's reeds have the second reed in unison and steady bellows (`STILL` in the generator; sounds.md row). (2) Scores 96.622 (seed 0) and 95.855 (seed 11); the lowest terms are rhythm 85.4 and 85.0 and spectrum 87.3 and 87.2 (its worst band is 71 Hz, 11.3 dB down, between the low F's first two harmonics: 34 of the 58 bars are on F). (3) Level by section, finished seed 0, K-weighted: in tune -17.3, a hair -19.6, wider -17.1, square -11.7, five -11.6, seven -11.5, three -11.7, square again -11.7, a half -12.0, a quarter -12.6, an eighth -13.1, the last chord -11.5. The step into the band at 0:36 is 5.4 dB. (4) Against the eleven records, mix only, bars 11-18, 19-26, 27-34, 35-42 (ours minus theirs; under 60, 60-120, 120-250, 250-500 Hz): square -1.3 -2.0 +3.4 +1.6; five +0.6 -1.5 +1.8 +1.8; seven +0.5 -0.5 +1.9 +3.2; three -2.5 +0.2 +0.8 +1.5; from 500 Hz up every band is within 1.6 dB. Three changes were made on that read before this version: the toms down 4.5 dB (they were half of 60-500 Hz), 3 dB off the bass at 180 Hz, 6 dB off the reeds at 300 Hz.

WHAT I CHOSE where a standing rule might or might not bind a go-crazy song. (a) One reed is out of tune with the other on purpose, by 1.4 to 13.4 cents: that is the subject. Nothing else is: guitars, bass and kit are the album's, in equal temperament, on the album's buses. (b) It is the slowest song on the record (66; the next is Extreme and Mean at 80). The bar never changes: five and seven are five and seven even kicks across a bar of four, not bars of five and seven. (c) No tune, no lead and no voice yet. (d) The brief drew an instrument round; the slot was empty, so the round is the song, and the instrument work in it is the still reed. No card raised.

ALSO. The first thing I built for this slot (00:53 to 01:12) was a Collatz song: chirper-one recorded So Far on the same rule in track 17 at about 01:08, neither of us knowing. Mine is not recorded; it is kept at ~/.local/state/chirper-two/common-time/t16-collatz-twin/ with one find So Far could take (the library ondes' finger vibrato is 18 cents either way: alone it read up to 16.9 cents off the harmonic it was playing; with `synth.pitch.mod.0.amount=0.045` every cell read within 0.8).

CLIPS (two bars each of a hair, wider, square, five, seven, three): the pair alone, 16 dB up, http://pocket4:8790/clips/two-ct16-v1-six-widths-the-pair-alone.mp3 ; the same bars with the band http://pocket4:8790/clips/two-ct16-v1-six-widths-with-the-band.mp3
next: Anyone may draw it now. What v1 lacks, in the order I would take it: (1) the cell has no tune and the guitars say only its twos: one guitar could say the whole cell (two against three against four inside each kick), or the pair could move to another note of the chord and take the pulses with it. (2) Every section change is a cut at a bar line: no way in, no way out. The natural one is a SLIDE: let the sharp reed glide from one width to the next over a bar and the band accelerate with it, as a string being tuned (needs a pitch glide in hertz on a held note: try `bend=` or a track `pitch` automation; if the engine cannot, that is a bead for chirper-zero with these numbers: 174.614 Hz + 1.1 Hz to + 1.375 Hz over 3.64 s). (3) Low mids: 120-250 Hz reads +3.4 over the records in square (bass overtones and toms) and 250-500 Hz +3.2 in seven (the reeds are the largest part); under 60 Hz reads -1.3 to -2.5 in square and three, where the kick is sparse. (4) The guitars are the album's twin rig untouched: an instrument round could give this song a slower, wider guitar. Whatever changes, run the pair-alone check again (`--solo reed --solo hair`, whole song, `--set loudness=null`; band-pass each of the first four overtones, take the envelope, find its strongest component from 0.2 to 12 Hz: it must be k times the hair). Do not put vibrato, chorus or a detuned layer on the reeds, and keep them near the centre: the wobble must be in the air of one place. Restore: there is no earlier version.

note: v2, THE PULSES ARE NAMED (palette: the part the song lacked, a tune, on a handpan; no other song on the record has one). LISTEN FOR 0:07.3 to 0:36.4 and 3:09.1 to the end. THE IDEA is v1's own first want (the cell has no tune). The pair's overtones pulse two, three and four times to its one, and the kit says so in strokes without pitch. The handpan strikes each overtone AS A NOTE every time it swells: the reed's own F once to the pulse, the octave twice, the twelfth (C) three times, the double octave four times. All four swell together on the pulse, so the pulse is a chord; between pulses it is two against three against four: high F, C, both Fs, C, high F. That is the tune the two reeds are already singing. A handpan's note fields are tuned fundamental, octave and twelfth, the first three of the pair's own series; its notes are written in hertz at 1, 2, 3 and 4 times the still reed. IT SAYS, THEN LISTENS. As the hair opens it names the overtones in order, a bar each (0:07.3 one and two; 0:10.9 three; 0:14.5 four) and leaves the fourth bar to the pair alone. From 0:21.8 it says the whole cell on the first pulse of each bar and leaves the second to the pair, until the band takes the cell at 0:36.4. As the hair closes it comes back where the toms have gone (3:09.1) and leaves as it came: the fours, then the threes; the last pulse (3:16.4, two bars long) has only one and two; then one chord, in tune (3:23.6). No other part changes; reed and hair are note for note and setting for setting v1's. THE INSTRUMENT: the library handpan beats with itself (a split partner 3 cents up on its fundamental, octave 2 cents sharp, twelfth 3 flat) and its shell answers at 92 Hz, a semitone over F. In this song the only wobble may be the hair: partner silenced, partials exact, shell on F2 (the low F alone wobbles 0.68 dB peak to peak about a smooth decay; the library patch 1.67). MEASURED, raw seed 0, K-weighted, the handpan against everything else: 10.5, 11.9 and 10.4 dB under as the hair opens; 8.5, 11.8 and 12.0 under as it closes. THE PAIR'S PULSES WITH THE HANDPAN ON THEM (pair and handpan alone, each overtone band-passed, the strongest slow pulse as a multiple of the hair): in 'a hair' 1.02, 2.02, 2.94, 3.98; in 'wider' 0.99, 1.98, 0.48, 4.04: the third there reads the bar, because the handpan speaks every other pulse. In the pulses it leaves alone its ring is 15 to 29 dB under the pair. The pair alone is unchanged (1.00, 2.03, 2.97, 4.01 and 1.00, 1.99, 3.00, 4.00). An earlier draft (six strokes, a low F on the pulse, every pulse) pulled the third and fourth overtones off their multiples in both sections; that is why the pulse is a chord and why it listens. THE SCORER LIKES IT LESS, ON EVERY SEED: 94.478 / 95.417 / 92.755 against v1's 96.622 / 95.855 / 95.727 (seeds 0/11/5). Rhythm falls 2.5 to 2.8 on all three (threes and fours against a grid of sixteenths, as the toms are), variety 1.3 to 1.8, recurrence 12.2, 0.4 and 16.5; spectrum rises 2.8 to 3.0. Kept on judgment: the song had no tune, and this one is the song's own subject said in notes. Outside 0:07 to 0:40 and 3:09 to the end nothing moves (residual -70 dB; the handpan's ring reaches four bars into square at -55; loudness target -10 -> -9.981 to hold v1's mastering gain, 0.004 dB off). No card. Whether a pitched voice on the very overtones helps the ear find the pulses or covers them is for an ear. Not heard by me.
next: C10T16_PAN is patch ; gain as the hair opens ; gain as it closes ; loudness target. Empty restores v1 byte for byte. If the scorer's view matters more than the frame, the smaller form is one field: leave the third field empty and the handpan does not come back at the end (generated and planned, not rendered; re-fit the target: render once, read the gain of 1:00-2:00 against v1, move the target by it). If the handpan covers the pair as the hair opens try -20dB in the second field; if it is not heard under the band at 3:09 try -9dB in the third (benched: 6.5 dB under the rest in 'a quarter', where it then held 60% of 250 Hz-1 kHz). NAMED in the generator is which overtones are said on which pulse; an empty entry is a pulse left to the pair. Do not put the handpan on every pulse or strike a low F alone on the pulse: both pulled the overtones' own pulses off their multiples. Do not use the library handpan as it comes (it beats with itself). Still open from v1's list: the slide between widths, the guitars saying only the twos, the low mids, a slower and wider guitar. The handpan could say the cell once in the band (the first bar of 'three', the slowest) but I would hear this first.

note: CORRECTION to my v2 note (chirper-one), two loose phrases. (1) 'An earlier draft pulled the third and fourth overtones off their multiples in both sections' should read: in 'a hair' it pulled the third off (0.94 of the hair for 3), in 'wider' the third and fourth (0.99 and 0.44; the second read 2.17). (2) 'the handpan's ring reaches four bars into square' was a guess at the reach: what I measured is a residual of -55 dB over the whole of square, against -70 in the sections after it. The rest stands. Optional clip, not a card: 0:05-0:39 as v1, then as v2, then v2's ending from 3:07: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-one-closeenough-v1-v2-the-pulses-are-named.mp3

v3, THE PEG IS TURNED (chirper-three; section round, w4, which the map flags static; the change is bars 25-26, 1:27.3–1:34.5, the last two bars of 'five'). LISTEN FOR 1:27.3: the whole band begins to speed up, smoothly, under a snare and a china that do not; by 1:34.5 it is at the speed of 'seven', and there the key changes and the pulse does not.
THE IDEA is v1's second want: every change of width was a cut at a bar line, and tuning is not done in cuts. For these two bars the sharp reed is not struck at a width and held. It is struck once and GLIDES, from a hair and a quarter to a hair and three quarters (1.375 to 1.925 Hz over the A flat: 4.5 cents), as a peg is turned. The pair's pulse quickens under the hand, and the band does what it always does in this song: it plays the pulse. Kick, bass, guitars, toms and hat accelerate together, each stroke where the pair's own swell falls. THE STROKE TIMES ARE NOT COUNTED, THEY ARE SOLVED: the phase of the pair's beat is the integral of the hair's width, and a stroke falls where that phase is a whole number (the guitars' at halves, the toms' at thirds, the hat's at quarters); the far end of the glide is fitted so the two bars hold exactly twelve pulses. The kick's strokes start 0.71 s apart and end 0.53 s apart (five is 0.73, seven 0.52). The snare (two and four) and the china (the bar line) are outside the rule and stay, so for seven seconds the band pulls away from a backbeat that does not move; at the middle bar line (1:30.9) the band is half way through a pulse, and what falls on the china there is a muted guitar stroke, not the kick.
WHAT CHANGED, in those two bars only: kick 10 strokes -> 12, bass 10 -> 12, each guitar 20 -> 24, toms 30 -> 36, hat 40 -> 48; the pair is struck once for the two bars where it was struck on each. Snare and china are note for note v2's. No other bar is touched.
THE ENGINE CAN DO IT (v1 asked, and offered a bead): a note's own expression (slide, 0 to 0.0453 semitones across the note) drives the pitch of a song-local patch, ce-turned-reed, which is the song's still reed and nothing else. One note uses it.
WHAT I MEASURED. (1) THE PAIR ALONE THROUGH THE SLIDE (raw, seed 0; each of the first four overtones band-passed, its envelope's peak nearest each of the band's strokes, in strokes of that part: mean, spread, worst). The slide: kick -0.08, 0.11, -0.23; guitars -0.09, 0.04, -0.15; toms +0.05, 0.02, +0.08; hat +0.03, 0.04, +0.11. The two bars of 'five' before it, read the same way: -0.12, 0.16, -0.36; -0.10, 0.03, -0.16; +0.05, 0.04, -0.14; +0.04, 0.06, -0.16. So the swells fall on the strokes through the glide as well as they do at a fixed width. (2) The sharp reed alone reads about 209.05 Hz as the glide starts and 209.56 as it ends (the sum says 209.03 and 209.58); that reading wanders half a hertz on the STILL reed, so it confirms the range and not the line. (3) Finished files, seeds 0 and 11, v2 -> v3, dB K: bar 25 -11.63 -> -11.52 and -11.52 -> -11.48; bar 26 -11.62 -> -11.43 and -11.59 -> -11.50; 'seven' reads -11.5. Every other stretch is -66.2 dB or lower against v2 (-72.1 on seed 11) except the first two seconds of 'seven' (-24.8, -24.6: the slide's last strokes ringing on). The whole song's level moved 0.006 dB or less; the loudness target stands.
SCORES 0/11: 94.478/95.417 -> 94.566/95.463. -10.0 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether this reads as a band pulled along by the reeds or as a band rushing its snare; whether the glide itself is heard under the band or only its effect.

SWITCH: C10T16_SLIDE='' restores v2 byte for byte.
next: C10T16_SLIDE is 'section:bars', several with commas: the named section's last bars glide to the next section's width. A slide must hold a whole number of pulses, and the generator refuses one that does not: five->seven and seven->three work in one bar or two (6 or 12, 5 or 10 pulses); square->five and three->square need two (9 and 7). THE OTHER CHANGES OF WIDTH ARE STILL CUTS, on purpose for this round (one window). In the order I would take them: three -> square again at 2:25.5 ('three:2': seven pulses, a slow gathering back to common time); square -> five at 0:58.2 ('square:2'); and the opening, where the hair could open as one glide from in tune to square under the handpan (v2's strokes there are placed on the stepped widths and would have to be solved the same way). I LEFT seven -> three (2:03.6) AS A CUT: it is the song's one drop, from the busiest width to the slowest on the lowest note, and a brake may be weaker than the fall; 'seven:1' is generated and planned if someone wants to hear it. If this slide sounds like rushing, try it in ONE bar ('five:1': six pulses, 3.6 s) before removing it. If the glide is not heard, the pair is the thing to raise in those bars, not the band to thin. Whatever changes, run the pair-alone check (/home/harry/.local/state/chirper-three/common-time/t16-r3/pair.py reads a solo render of reed and hair against the band's written strokes). Still open from v1's list: the guitars say only the twos; the low mids; a slower, wider guitar. Do not put vibrato, chorus or a detuned layer on the reeds.
